units: pixels (image coords, x right, y DOWN) and seconds; no metric scale assumed
summary: Indoor basketball court, camera facing the end wall. A woman (cap, beige tank top, olive cargo pants, white sneakers) holds a basketball, dips, tosses it nearly straight up (slightly to the right) with a small jump, the ball rises to near the top of the frame and falls back, she catches it, then drops/dribbles it once: it bounces on the floor (frame 77), travels left and bounces again (frame 102) while she walks right and then back left.

camera.drift_rate: dy grows ~0.45-0.6 px/frame during frames 10-60, slows to ~0.1-0.2 px/frame after frame 80; dx < 4.4 px always
camera.scale_change: image scale 0.994-1.000 relative to frame 0 (<=0.6 %), rotation < 0.1 deg
camera.usage: frame-0 (stabilised) coords = raw + (dx_to_f0_px, dy_to_f0_px) to within ~1 px; full affine m00..m12 maps raw frame-i pixel to frame-0 pixel. Background content moves UP in the image over time (backboard top y 137 at f0 -> ~102 at f112).
camera.measured_from: ORB features on the wall/backboard/scoreboard (floor and person/ball zones masked), RANSAC similarity transform to frame 0

perspective.view: roughly frontal to the end wall; wall plane ~parallel to image plane
perspective.note: lane lines are perpendicular to the wall; their vanishing point ~(903,595) ~ horizon height y~595 at frame 0 (camera at about person chest height). Objects on different depth planes (ball near player vs. wall/backboard) do NOT share one scale; ball, player are roughly at the same depth (ball diameter grows from ~50 to ~53-55 px late in the clip as it comes toward the camera after the dribble).
